blocks.x: Trial eligibility matching at 10x — enrollment windows met

A European biopharma group — a Healthcare & Life Sciences engagement delivered by a blended Dataq Software team under the outcome-linked engagement model. Identity withheld as standard; the figures are the client's, reproduced with permission.
Eligibility matching ran on chart review; two trials missed enrollment windows at a cost of years.
RWE pipelines rebuilt per study; regulatory-grade provenance missing. Discovery screening compute-bound on HPC with unclear quantum relevance.

We built the eligibility engine: protocol criteria translated to governed EHR queries with evidence bundles for each candidate, plus a Quanta pilot benchmarking screening formulations against classical baselines (verdict: parity at current scale — documented). RWE pipelines moved to reusable, provenance-complete templates.
What the success is actually made of

items: one governed definition per metric ended the metric disputes before the build scaled.
every automated action carried its policy version and its trail, which is why operations trusted the fleet by month three.
formulation discipline carried the value: the same discipline that says no when the numbers do not support the method.

blocks.x: The pattern behind the European biopharma group program travels; the estate does not. Teams considering this path should expect the diagnostic to reshape scope at least once — that is the process working, not failing The engagement model here was build-transfer; the same pattern runs fixed-scope where the estate allows it.
Figures on this page are the client's, reproduced with permission. Method notes and measurement designs are available under NDA.
Start with the diagnostic, not the contract: the same diagnostic baselined in two weeks, and a scoped proposal only if the delta justifies it.
